amended.summary: Table-2 false-admit figures (dependency 1.30%, count 5.52%) are reported under two named definitions, not a bare rate. Definition A (gate's own documented predicate, witnessed reference-existence): all three structural arms 0-false-admit (dependency 0/23702, count 0/163, negation 0/163). Definition B (bench's stricter, undocumented CALL-only label): dependency 309/23702=1.30%, count 9/163=5.52%, negation 0/163=0%, relation 452/452=100%. Line-by-line adjudication of all 318 Definition-B rows found 0/318 genuine unsoundness -- every one is a labelling gap between the bench's isCallee check and the gate's reference-existence predicate, not an unwitnessed admit. Recall figures are unaffected and unchanged. No bench run was repeated; all figures trace to the artifact already committed at 99575cd plus code read at the cited file:line locations.

falseAdmit_two_definitions.definitionA: unsoundness under the gate's own documented predicate: verifyDependency (packages/genesis/src/verify-fact.ts:96) admits on reverseCallers(target) intersect sourceScope != empty; reverseCallers (packages/index/src/symbol-reverse.ts:120, 'if (occ.role !== "reference") continue;') counts ANY SCIP reference occurrence (import/type-position/instanceof-operand/re-export) as a witness, not only a call. verifyCount (packages/genesis/src/verify-count.ts:84-90) proves the same lower bound over the same witness set. Unsound under A = admitted with ZERO reference witness in the flipped scope.
falseAdmit_two_definitions.definitionB: mismatch vs the bench's CALL-only label: isCallee (packages/adapter-io/test/support/neg-bench-lib.ts:81-84) labels FALSE only when the target has no CallExpression/NewExpression callee occurrence in scope; it does not check references. A row can be Def-B-false while Def-A-true.
falseAdmit_two_definitions.adjudication: all 318 Def-B rows (309 dependency + 9 count) adjudicated line-by-line, cold-seat-verified, spot-cold-checked against source: 0/318 genuine unsoundness. dependency: 309/309 have a real non-definition SCIP reference occurrence of the target in scope, corroborated by tsc's own refFiles; 0/309 have a call in scope. Of these, 2 also trip the bench's separate whole-program call-eligibility proxy (callFiles>0 anywhere, not necessarily in-scope): isGrounded (witness: import at packages/adapter-io/src/compose.ts:24) and DegenerateAnchorError (witness: import at packages/adapter-io/src/governed-promote.ts:54, instanceof operand at :111) -- both witnesses are references, never calls, same gap class as the other 307. count: 9/9 are boundary cases where atLeast == in-scope-call-count + 1 while in-scope references (the gate's actual witness set) >= atLeast.

dependency_false_admits_call_eligible.reading: AMENDED (WP-C3, 2026-08-18): the original 'reading' here called this a 'residual real unsoundness' -- that was itself an overclaim, corrected by row-level adjudication. Both call_eligible_symbols are witnessed ONLY by reference occurrences (compose.ts:24 import; governed-promote.ts:54 import + :111 instanceof), never by a call, in the flipped scope. callFiles>0 means tsc found a call SOMEWHERE in the whole program, not necessarily in the scope the claim asserts -- it is a different, looser proxy than the in-scope witness the gate actually checks, and the bench's own tighter in-scope check (0/309 have an in-scope call) is definitive. This is Definition B (mismatch vs bench's call label), not Definition A (gate's own reference predicate, on which these 2 rows are also sound: 0 unwitnessed). The shipped AC-6 assertion FAILS because it is written to Definition B (see test_suite_result), not because the door admitted an unwitnessed fact.

scope_limit_disclaimer: SOUND HEADLINE = structural arms only (count / dependency / negation vs the independent tsc oracle). The relation arm is MEASURED, not guaranteed (no direction oracle: admitRelation has no way to reject a reversed edge, so both falseAdmit and recallTrue print 100% by construction). Semantic slots (invariant / sideeffect / advisory prose) tsc cannot witness are NOT covered here at all.
limits: recall over PLANTED mutations on a synthetic-labelled fixture, not recall over arbitrary real-world facts
covers only the 4 oracle-bearing shapes (count, relation, dependency, negation); advisory/predicate prose has no sound oracle and is out of scope

recall is INDEX-BUILD-DEPENDENT by roughly an order of magnitude (count/dependency recall 4.29% dist-absent vs 100% dist-form; negation recall 4.25% vs 35.67%) — a bare percentage without the build recipe is not a citable number

the fixture pin's `substrate.rev` field says `e35dcce`, an OLDER commit than this worktree's HEAD (9eb4d7f). The pin's own comment clarifies the tsc oracle is 'a deterministic pure function of the checked-out src at this rev' (i.e. whatever is checked out, not the pinned annotation), and nothing in AC-7 enforces that the checked-out src matches `e35dcce` — only the SYNTHETIC self-proof fixture bytes (semantic-bench-fixture.json) are hash-pinned, not the substrate. So the numbers in this report are for 9eb4d7f, not e35dcce, and that drift is exactly why the doc's committed AC-6 comments (e.g. 'dependency = 0.08% residual...17/23577') no longer match this run's Definition-B counts (18/23702 dist-absent, 309/23702 dist-form) — the population grew and the assertion's Definition-B check now trips on this larger population, per the correction above. This is worth flagging to the code owner, not something I fixed (out of scope for a measurement WP).
